I just got my replacement Squape Reloaded glass today. Again. This is the second glass section on this tank that I've killed. My first replacement scheme went according to the (then and still) Swiss instructions from Stattqualm, which included using a vice. That should have been my first clue it wouldn't go right. Long story short, I got the included block of wood stuck in there and managed to kill all threads on my tank section. 0/10, would not do again.

I ended up buying the tank section of my friend's off of him, as he was willing to get a colored section. I merrily went on my way enjoying my new Squape tank section until tragedy struck. The Squape R and ZNA combo - which I am in love with to this day - jumped out of my pocket and onto the cruel Carolina asphalt on my way to my car. A small pebble struck and perforated my glass, shattering my heart once again. I powered through for a few days using the new cotton Aspire Nautilus BVC coils, and purchased an Erlprinz for something that was cheaper and less likely to shatter (despite the metal cage on the Squape R).

My glass arrived today. Was I willing to risk my tank again? Yes. Because I'm not known for making great decisions.

First, I replaced the two O-rings on the inside of my Squape, which is a bitch and a half. I've never had to replace interior O-rings before, so that probably played into it. Then I lubed them up with my sweet sweet Nanner Bear.

I got the glass. The French video shows that the wood block should be asymmetrical; one end will fit inside the tank and the other will not. Like my last one, neither side fit. Not going in a good direction so far. I called VapeRev customer support for emotional support, applied some more Nanner Bear to the frosted glass, and put on the included finger condom. I gently pushed it through and was able to get over the first O-ring with some force. The glass swiftly came to a halt. It moved so fast, I thought I might have gotten both O-rings in one go, and let the all-too-nice VapeRev customer service agent go because I thought I was done.

I was not done. The second O-ring didn't get fully covered. I tested to make sure it was on there by covering the drip tip hole with a finger and blowing. I could feel the air escaping and I heard my precious juice bubbling away. I kept twisting at it, but the finger condom tore. Was it over so soon? Still no. It never ends.

I tried work gloves, things wrapped in towels, all to no avail. I could hear the air escaping. When, suddenly, a less than brilliant idea came to mind. I have a bunch of 18350s lying around that I never use anymore...

So I pulled out an 18350. It fit perfectly. My descent into total idiocy was almost complete. In a stroke of common sense, I decided to rest my negative end against the glass. That way, if the wrapper shreds, I won't vent a lovely battery all over my bathroom. Probably.

Firmly, but cautiously, I kept pressing in. The glass forcefully descended and stopped. I checked for cracks. I checked for rips in the wrapper. I checked for bubbles. None.

She's wicked and ready to go, and even though it's been only five days since I last used her.

Holy shitballs. Did I miss this tank. Review incoming.

Science worship. Some people seriously overestimate the power of science and/or think that science can resolve any issue. What they do not understand is that science is simply a process. It utilizes the scientific method in attempt of seeking true knowledge, but that does not mean that it is true.

Some experiments need to be repeated by other scientists to see if a previous study was accurate or even measuring what the investigator said they were measuring; some conclusions that scientists arrive at are false; some scientists interpret data in a way that "proves* their hypothesis; and a number of other problems. Scientists are only human.

One of the larger issues is where people get their information from. The media is notoriously bad for misinterpreting scientific studies, ex. when "cures" are found. Sometimes with the use of a perfectly reliable and accurate source, a journalist may spout speculations or pseudo-science that was not even concluded from the study that they cite. Even worse is that the media doesn't always know how to tell a good study from a bad one, or simply don't care because the bad one may be "newsworthy".

Now don't get me wrong, I am not anti-science nor am I religiously biased. I just don't like the spread of misinformation or the bullshit argument of "because science!".

"accept that intelligence is at least partially genetic"... Thats a pretty huge assumption. It's more accurate to say that families pass down social and cultural capital that contribute to the future intelligence of their children. It's dangerous to call that an aspect of genetics.

> Thats a pretty huge assumption.

It's really not. Personally, I am of the view that raw intelligence (the g factor, as measured by IQ tests) is almost entirely genetic; cognitive scientist Steven Pinker agrees, and has several excellent papers, books, and very accessible videos discussing the subject. The 'blank slate' idea has been proven false for a long time. Try https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CuQHSKLXu2c

The social and cultural capital that results in better education does indeed provide excellent thinking tools and knowledge, but ultimately it is the raw intelligence that determines how much of this can be absorbed and used and understood. This intelligence is selected for genetically like any other trait: if it helps you thrive, it survives.

Sorry for the late reply! Totally forgot voat was a thing. I just don't think we should consider the "g-factor" as proof of genetic intelligence. All we know is that "g" is heritable but that could also be due to environmental reasons. For example, a father and son might have the same "g" score because they were raised identically. I mean, some psychometricians don't even believe that intelligence can be explained with a single factor model. Some things to note: The g factor is a statistical construct obtained through a process called factor analysis. Without getting into the nitty-gritty of it, its a pretty subjective method. Depending on how you choose your factors (i.e. scree test, keiser-gutman rule, chi-square test, etc.), you can end up with any number of models that explain intelligence. Just because some people think a single factor (g) explains intelligence, it doesn't mean the whole community agrees. The g factor is merely a statistical construct that is positively correlated with IQ tests but itself is not a metric for intelligence nor does it definitely indicate intelligence genes.
